MARISA T. TUAZON HON. CARL GERARD CASTILLO HON. NELSON CARMELO V. LUCIANO HON. JESUS B. DE GUZMAN, JR. Sangguniang Bayan Members Santa Maria, Bulacan Dear Honorable SB Members: This pertains to your letter dated January 29, 2024 concerning the alleged irregularities for non-observance of the Internal Rules of Procedure (IRP) of the Sangguniang Bayan of Santa Maria, Bulacan. In your letter, you represented that the subject IRP was adopted by the Sanggunian on September 22, 2022 under Resolution No. 2022-038, entitled: THE NEW INTERNAL RULES OF PROCEDURE FOR THE REMAINING PERIOD OF THE TERM OF THE 1 ITH SANGGUNIANG BAYAN OF SANTA MARIA, BULACAN. The said IRP was religiously followed by all the members of the Sangguniang Bayan since its approval until the move to repeal the same last January 11, 2024. However, in a privilege speech delivered by SB Member Mark Angelo R. Clemente, he alleged that there were inconsistencies and illegalities in the existing IRP, such allegations were contested as you represented that the same is malicious. You intimated that during the flow of the discussion, Vice Mayor Pablo L. Juan manipulated the floor and led his "kapartido" SB Members to make manifestation, in the guise of asking clarificatory questions but basically leading to a well-orchestrated plan of changing the IRP to fit their move as the majority of the members with utter disregard of parliamentary process. The gist of the discussion focuses on whether the IRP should be repealed or amended. Since there were only three (3) pinpointed sections to change per the privilege speech of SB Member Clemente, your view is that, the IRP should only be amended. Hence, the instant request. At the outset, the Supreme Court in the case of Romulo vs. Yfiiquezl has ruled that IRPs are not laws but are simply procedural rules to be observed by the Sangguniang for its orderly conduct of sessions and thus, it can be waived, disregarded or suspended by the deliberative body. 1 L-71908 dated February 4, 1986 "Matino, Mahusay, at Maaasahan" Trunkline: (02) 8876-3454

Rules are hardly permanent in character, they are subject to revocation, modification or waiver at the pleasure of the body adopting them as they are primarily procedural. IRPs of the Sanggunian do not have the imprints of permanence and obligatoriness during their effectivity since it does not have the force of law but merely in the nature of by-laws designed for the orderly and convenient proceedings2. But while internal rules and generally waivable by the sanggunian, the rules provided for by the Constitution or statutes are non-waivable. Thus, unless the Constitution or the statute is violated, the court will not interfere therewith and legislative act will not be declared invalid, simply, for non-compliance with the internal rules, rather than any constitutional or statutory requirement3. Accordingly, we are of the considered view that the IRP, may thus, be amended and/or repealed. Be that as it may, this Department enjoins the Sangguniang Bayan Members of Santa Maria, Bulacan to thresh this matter in the most civilized manner, putting premium on the harmonious relationship of each local legislator and the respect of the rule of law. This opinion shall be without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you Very truly yours, BY A T RITY OF THE SECRETARY: .J OR R. LLAMAS cretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs ELLA/JVRULLLS-LRALLD/rrao Copy furnished: ATTY. ANTHONY C.
